headline: The Pentagon says it has stopped using Anthropic's AI tools, months after labelling the company a national-security supply-chain risk.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a Pentagon statement that it has dropped a leading AI lab's tools, with sources saying use went on until last week, but it rests on one outlet and unnamed sources.
importance_line: Pentagon analysts lose an AI tool that sources say sat inside their main intelligence platform, and Anthropic loses its Pentagon work, but the account comes from one outlet and unnamed sources, and the reason for the delay is unclear.
summary: The BBC reports that a Pentagon official said on 5 Oct 2026 that the department "has ceased the use of Anthropic products", a full halt the BBC says had not been reported before, although people familiar with the matter say Anthropic's Claude AI model was still used last week for intelligence work and in military operations against Iran. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth labelled Anthropic a supply-chain risk in February, a label usually applied to firms from hostile countries, after it refused to drop its safety limits, citing mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, and he set a late-August deadline for ending Pentagon use; Anthropic is suing to overturn the label.
notes: Read the full BBC article (prefetched text). Follow-up of the 3 Oct ABC News report on the court fight (pool item 1004:C13-04, never printed). Palantir and the Maven platform appear in the facts file and the importance line only, to keep the summary short.
